nodes.summary: HKA's divergence variance is positive for `θ > 0`, `T ≥ 0`, `f > -1`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the HKA divergence variance

nodes.summary: HKA's variance of the divergence, `θ (T + (1 + f) / 2) + (θ (1 + f) / 2)²`.
nodes.title: HKA variance of the divergence

nodes.summary: The true parameters solve HKA's estimating equations at the expected counts.
nodes.title: True parameters solve the HKA estimating equations

nodes.summary: HKA's estimating equations (Hudson, Kreitman & Aguadé 1987) for parameters `θ i`, `T`, `f` given the counts: the totals over loci of polymorphism in `A`, in `B` and of divergence match their expectations, and at each locus the total of the three counts matches its expectation. (Only `L - 1` of the per-locus equations are independent of the totals.)
nodes.title: HKA's estimating equations

nodes.summary: HKA's expected number of segregating sites `θ C(n)` in a sample of `n` genes with scaled mutation rate `θ` (use `f θ` for species `B`).
nodes.title: HKA expected number of segregating sites

nodes.summary: HKA's variances are positive in the biological domain: `θ > 0`, `n ≥ 2`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the HKA polymorphism variance

nodes.summary: HKA's variance of the number of segregating sites, `θ C(n) + θ² C₂(n)`.
nodes.title: HKA variance of the number of segregating sites

nodes.summary: The HKA statistic for `L` loci with polymorphism counts `SA i`, `SB i`, divergences `D i`, parameters `θ i`, `T`, `f` and sample sizes `nA`, `nB`: the sum over loci of the squared standardized deviations of the three counts from their HKA expectations.
nodes.title: Hudson–Kreitman–Aguadé statistic

nodes.summary: Expected divergence (Hudson, Kreitman & Aguadé 1987): if the ancestral coalescence time `τ` is exponential with rate `2 / (1 + f)` and, given the genealogy σ-algebra `m`, the divergence `D` has conditional mean `θ (T + τ)`, then `E D = θ (T + (1 + f) / 2)` (for `f > -1`). No integrability hypothesis on `D` is needed: if `D` were not integrable its conditional expectation would be `0` (Mathlib's convention), and the…
nodes.title: Expected divergence

nodes.summary: If every count is square integrable with the HKA mean and variance (as derived above under the neutral model), with `θ i > 0`, `T ≥ 0`, `f > 0` and `nA, nB ≥ 2`, then `E X² = 3 L`.
nodes.title: The HKA statistic has mean `3 L` at the true parameters

nodes.summary: Variance of the divergence (Hudson, Kreitman & Aguadé 1987): under the hypotheses of `integral_hkaDivergence`, if moreover `D` is square integrable with conditional variance `θ (T + τ)` given `m` (as for a Poisson count), then `Var D = θ (T + (1 + f) / 2) + (θ (1 + f) / 2)²`.
nodes.title: Variance of the divergence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
